title: Robots as professional Chefs - Nikhil Abraham, CloudChef
talk_summary: CloudChef trains a general-purpose two-armed wheeled robot to be a professional line cook by combining robot foundation models, teleoperation fallback, and cooking-specific thermal/visual embeddings, with recipes modeled as state machines. Their key claim is that private domain data (thermal sensors in real kitchens) beats frontier models like Gemini 2.5 and o3 on cooking-state estimation, and that a 95% autonomous / 5% teleoperated mix is faster and more reliable than either alone.

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a task-specific eval (estimate cooking progress from live feed) and found their small specialized perception model outperformed expert human chefs and frontier models, attributing the gap to a missing modality (thermal) that has no internet-scale data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when we put like state-of-the-art models like Gemini 2.5 or 03, they actually perform way worse than our own models
takeaways.numbers: tiny model beats expert chefs paid >$150k/yr and beats Gemini 2.5 / o3 on progress estimation

takeaways.technique: Specialized small model over general frontier model for narrow perception
takeaways.what_they_do: They fine-tuned small models on private domain data for a narrow perception task rather than calling a general frontier model, because the frontier model lacked the relevant modality/data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they don't have any thermal modality. And the thing is thermal modality does not have internet scale data

takeaways.what_they_do: The system runs ~95% autonomous and falls back to human teleoperation for edge cases, which they say is faster and more reliable than either pure autonomy or pure teleop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: about 95% autonomous, 5% teleyoperated. And it's way faster and way more reliable than just teleyop or just foundation models

takeaways.technique: State-machine task modeling with progress estimation
takeaways.what_they_do: Recipes are modeled as state machines over perception embeddings, so the system always knows which step it is on and whether it is done, enabling progress tracking and resumption.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've basically modeled recipes as state machines based on these embedding models at the core

takeaways.technique: Exploit idle capacity for batch work
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the robot as long as the facility operates and schedule prep/chopping tasks overnight when the line is idle.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are some tasks that you can do overnight. So once we get into cutting, chopping etc. The robot will just be doing that overnight
takeaways.numbers: robot can work 168 hours/week vs 40 for a human

takeaways.technique: Blind human taste-test as ground-truth benchmark
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmark against a chef's own recreation via blind taste tests rather than chemical consistency, because the real target is 'better than a chef's second attempt.'
takeaways.evidence_quote: we get a chef to cook a recipe once and then we get our system ... recreate that recipe a couple of times and then we do blind taste tests
